items.question: How can scriptural and other treasures arise from mere conceptual construction?
premises: Scriptural treasures appear to be rooted in conceptual construction.
All awareness is made of the light of consciousness.
What is made of consciousness-light is not merely a conceptual construction.
items.inference: Therefore scriptural treasures cannot be merely products of conceptual construction but must be grounded in consciousness.
items.plain_english: If the riches of scripture and the rest were rooted only in conceptual construction, how could they arise? The answer is that all awareness is made of the light of consciousness.

items.question: What is the essential nature of the light that shines as awareness?
premises: Awareness is connected with the nature of light.
Because of that connection, it is essentially dense with conscious reflective awareness.
The light that shines has reflective awareness as its own nature.
items.inference: Therefore the shining of light is inseparable from self-reflective consciousness.
items.plain_english: Because it is of the nature of light, awareness is essentially dense with conscious self-reflection; and that light which shines has reflective awareness as its very nature.

rows.grounds: compound: para + vāc + devatā + viddha; describes the qualified person

items.question: Why should that reflective light not itself be the flood of scriptures?
premises: The self-reflective light is the essence of awareness.
Scriptural knowledge does not ultimately depend on external displays of reasoning.
One pierced by the supreme goddess of speech abides in that reflective light.
items.inference: Therefore that reflective light itself can be the flood of scriptures for one awakened by supreme speech.
items.plain_english: Why should that very light not be the flood of scriptures? What need is there for other displays of reasoning? One who is pierced by the supreme goddess of speech would simply abide in that.

rows.grounds: compound: laukika + māyīya + varṇa + puñja + vicitrita; negated description

items.question: Is the scriptural light variegated by ordinary worldly and māyic letters?
premises: The supreme scriptural light is not composed of worldly or māyic letter-clusters.
The revered Recognition teaching states that what abides in the self shines forth.
Self-abiding manifestation does not depend on external letter-forms.
items.inference: Therefore the true scriptural manifestation is an inner shining, not an arrangement of ordinary letters.
items.plain_english: But it is not variegated by masses of ordinary, māyic letters. As it is said in the revered Pratyabhijñā, what abides in the self shines forth of itself.

rows.grounds: governs tasmād in sense of separation from that

items.question: Can manifestation occur without reflective awareness of will?
premises: Reflective awareness of will proceeds in manifestation.
Knowers recognize reflective awareness as the nature of manifestation.
Without reflective awareness, manifestation would lack its own nature.
items.inference: Therefore manifestation necessarily includes reflective awareness and cannot occur without it.
items.plain_english: Reflective awareness of will does indeed proceed and is not absent from that. The wise know reflective awareness to be the very nature of manifestation; otherwise, manifestation would not be what it is.

rows.grounds: compound: ratna + ādi; instrumental of comparison

items.question: Is object-tinged light merely like an inert jewel, or does it involve conscious wonder?
premises: Light may appear object-tinged, like a jewel reflecting something.
Any reflective awareness falls within the range of the wonder of consciousness.
Conscious wonder distinguishes living awareness from inert reflection.
items.inference: Therefore even object-tinged manifestation is not merely inert but belongs to conscious reflective wonder.
items.plain_english: Even if light tinged by an object seems similar to jewels and the like, any reflective awareness at all belongs to the domain of the wonder of consciousness.

items.question: How does reflective awareness become clear in experiences like joy and pain?
premises: Reflective awareness can take joy, pain, and similar states as its objects.
Within that reflection there arises a surging inner grasp.
The surge of inner grasp makes the reflective awareness explicit.
items.inference: Therefore affective experiences become clear through the inner surge of reflective awareness.
items.plain_english: When reflective awareness has joy, pain, and the like as its objects, it becomes clear through the surging inner grasp that arises within that reflection.

items.question: How does an experience become fully clear and established?
premises: Reflective awareness becomes fully clear afterward through its inner development.
The teacher has stated that pleasure and similar states are established by one's own awareness.
What is established by one's own awareness stands firm without external proof.
items.inference: Therefore the clarity of experience is grounded in self-awareness.
items.plain_english: Afterward it attains full clearness. And so the teacher has said: pleasure and the like are established by one's own awareness and stand firm on that basis.

rows.grounds: compound: vyavasthā + samaya; locative of time
compound: svasaṃvit + sādhana; ablative of reason

items.question: Why must an experience be accepted as established by self-awareness even if not known that way at determination?
premises: At the time of later determination, the experience is not known in the same immediate way.
The experience is nevertheless established by self-awareness.
What is established by self-awareness must be accepted even when later conceptualized differently.
items.inference: Therefore self-awareness is the foundational proof of experience, prior to later determination.
items.plain_english: For at the time of later determination it is not known in that same way by self-awareness; even so, it must necessarily be accepted as established by self-awareness.

items.question: When does the level of universal non-difference become reflectively apprehended?
premises: The same process of later clarification applies here as well.
On the path of the rising of knowledge and related powers there is a level of universal non-difference.
That level becomes effective when it reaches reflective apprehension.
items.inference: Therefore the non-differentiated ground becomes manifest through reflective apprehension on the path of knowledge.
items.plain_english: So too here: afterward, on the path where knowledge and the other powers rise, the level consisting of universal non-difference comes to be reflectively apprehended.

rows.grounds: compound: tad + ucita + udāra + vimarśa + aṃśa + sphuṭatva; ablative of cause

items.question: How does the primordial emission attain the status of scripture?
premises: The non-differentiated level becomes reflectively apprehended.
A noble reflective portion fitting that level becomes clear.
When that clarity arises, the primordial emission takes on scriptural form.
items.inference: Therefore scripturehood arises when primordial emission becomes clearly reflective.
uncertainties: prāgvisargaḥ is doctrinally loaded; rendered literally as 'primordial emission'.
items.plain_english: Then, because a noble reflective portion fitting that level becomes clear, that very primordial emission attains the status of scripture.

items.question: Can any trace of practice be discerned even in the unconditioned supreme scriptural meaning?
premises: The supreme scriptural meaning is unconditioned.
Even there, some trace of practice can be discerned.
This supports the claim that scripture arises through reflective manifestation.
items.inference: Therefore the account of scripture as reflective manifestation is fitting, even at the supreme level.
items.plain_english: This indeed would be fitting, for even in the unconditioned supreme meaning of scripture some trace of practice can be discerned.

rows.grounds: refers to the trace of practice

items.question: How does a trace of practice develop into manifold scriptural powers?
premises: The trace of practice contains the future powers of knowledge and the rest in the abode of clearness.
Through coloring or conditioning, that trace becomes differentiated.
Differentiation expands it into manifold forms.
items.inference: Therefore the manifold powers of scripture unfold from an initially subtle trace through conditioning.
items.plain_english: That trace surely possesses the powers of knowledge and the rest that will arise in the abode of clearness; and from conditioning it becomes expanded into various manifold distinctions.

items.question: How can one reality appear in varied forms without losing its identity?
premises: A face appears differently in water, a mirror, a jewel, or a sword.
The appearances may be trembling, round, subtle, long, and so forth.
The variation belongs to the medium of manifestation, not to the face itself.
items.inference: Therefore the supreme reality can appear in manifold forms through different media without losing its nature.
items.plain_english: Just as a face appears in water, a mirror, a jewel, or a sword as trembling, round, subtle, long, and so on, so its manifestation varies with the medium.

items.question: What is the character of the treasures of knowledge in the supreme form?
premises: In the supreme form, treasures of knowledge arise.
They are beautiful with the unlimited triad of heart, seed, and self.
Their arising in the supreme form preserves their non-limited unity.
items.inference: Therefore the supreme treasures of knowledge are unified expressions of the heart-seed-self triad.
uncertainties: hṛdayabījātmatraya is a technical Trika triad; rendered literally.
items.plain_english: Thus, in the supreme form, the treasures of knowledge arise, beautiful with the unlimited triad of heart, seed, and self.

items.question: What happens when Bhairava, expanded by power, desires to emit the floods of beings?
premises: Bhairava is expanded by power.
He may desire to emit floods of beings.
Those beings arise as inner waves of his own surging form.
items.inference: Therefore manifestation of beings is an emission of Bhairava's own power, not an external creation.

items.question: What happens to the treasures of cognition when manifestation is emitted?
premises: The same treasures of cognition remain present at the moment of emission.
They take on a constraint born from limiting conditions.
That constraint appears as slight activity and practice.
items.inference: Therefore differentiated practice is an apparent conditioning of the same cognitive treasures, not a different reality.
items.plain_english: Then those very treasures of cognition, as if taking on a constraint of slight activity and practice born from that limiting condition,

items.question: Does assuming identity with the waves of manifestation alter the ground of awareness?
premises: The cognitive treasures appear to assume identity with the flood of waves.
This occurs within awareness-Bhairava.
Awareness-Bhairava remains beautiful with the bliss of the world.
items.inference: Therefore even apparent identification with manifested waves does not depart from the blissful ground of awareness.
items.plain_english: having assumed all around an identity with the flood of those waves, still remain within awareness-Bhairava, who is beautiful with the bliss of the world.

items.question: How can the power-holder state be set aside while power remains full?
premises: Awareness-Bhairava is satisfied with the mere fullness of being and possesses power.
By its own full power, the distinct state of the power-holder is set aside.
This setting aside occurs within the same powerful reality.
items.inference: Therefore the distinction between power and power-holder is an internal play of the one full power.
items.plain_english: In that powerful awareness, satisfied with the mere fullness of being, the state of the power-holder is set aside by its own full power alone.

items.question: What kind of knowledge stream unfolds when reflective awareness becomes dominant?
premises: A stream of knowledge whose nature is reflective awareness unfolds.
Within that stream, delight arises through the teaching of enjoyment.
The unfolding is not dry cognition but reflective and blissful.
items.inference: Therefore the unfolding of knowledge in this state is inseparable from reflective delight.
items.plain_english: Such a stream of knowledge, whose nature is reflective awareness, unfolds; and in it some delight arises through the teaching of enjoyment.

items.question: How can even enjoyment become a state of liberation for the fortunate?
premises: Enjoyment can be nourished by confidence in the conduct of awareness.
For the fortunate, this confidence transforms the meaning of enjoyment.
Transformed enjoyment no longer binds but leads to the highest good.
items.inference: Therefore even the multitude of enjoyments can become a path to liberation when grounded in awareness.
items.plain_english: For the fortunate, even the multitude of enjoyments, nourished by confidence in the practice of that awareness, becomes a state of supreme liberation.

items.question: What is said to be the deity's delight in worship in this context?
premises: A cited teaching describes the deity's delight in worship.
That delight is full of the stirring arousal of the deity's own primordial power.
It arises especially from among the Mothers.
items.inference: Therefore worship here is grounded in the arousal of the deity's own power, especially as expressed through the Mothers.
uncertainties: mātṛmadhyataḥ refers to the Mothers; specific group left literal.
items.plain_english: Here it is said that the deity's delight in worship is full of the stirring arousal of its own primordial power, especially arising from among the Mothers.

items.question: How is the deity of cognitive greatness manifested and unfolded?
premises: By the surge of sovereign power, the lordly state is obtained.
The deity whose greatness is cognition becomes manifested.
This manifestation is unfolded as the present teaching.
items.inference: Therefore the deity's unfolded form is the manifestation of sovereign cognitive power.
items.plain_english: By the surge of sovereign power, this deity, whose greatness is cognition and who has obtained the name of the lordly state, has become manifested and unfolded.

items.question: Why does the joining and separating of infinite portions of beings become countless?
premises: Infinite portions of beings are joined and separated.
This occurs through connection with the non-difference of the prior state.
The prior non-differentiated ground prevents any fixed numerical limit.
items.inference: Therefore the combinations of manifested beings are countless because they arise from a non-differentiated ground.
uncertainties: upāśrite is read as expressing attainment in this context; morphology is compact.
items.plain_english: Here too, in the joining and separating of infinite portions of beings, countlessness is attained because of the connection with the non-difference of the prior state.
